sections.overview: Asterias rubens is a common North-East Atlantic sea star that lives on the seabed.
sections.identification: It usually has five tapering arms and varies from orange or pale brown to violet.
sections.habitat: It occurs on varied seabeds, including rock, gravel and mussel beds, from the shore into deeper water.
sections.diet: It preys especially on bivalves, but also eats other invertebrates and carrion.
sections.behavior: Rows of tube feet help it move and handle prey; it can partly evert its stomach to digest food outside its body.
sections.reproduction: It releases eggs and sperm into the water, where fertilization takes place; spawning is seasonal in many populations.
sections.ecology: As a predator of mussels and other benthic animals, it can influence the local composition of seabed communities.
sections.conservation: Marine Life Information Network describes it as abundant across much of the North-East Atlantic; this does not imply that every local population is stable.
